prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "book", with the standing line "A small mdBook project that turns ten markdown chapters about the DALL·E server into a browsable static documentation site." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A stack of numbered markdown chapter sheets on the left, tilted in order, feeding rightward through a single squat press-like build step into one finished web page on the right, drawn at larger scale: that page shows a narrow chapter list down its left side, body text in the middle, and a small bordered outline panel pinned at its upper right. A thin line runs from the topmost chapter sheet, labelled as the table of contents, to the page's chapter list, showing that the order of the list comes from that one file. Two smaller sheets, a script and a stylesheet, join the build step from below.

Magnified circles set beside it show top circle, magnifying the finished page's body text with second-level headings marked and lines drawn from each heading to a matching entry in the outline panel. middle circle, the same outline panel with one entry filled solid as the reader scrolls past its heading. bottom circle, a narrow phone-width page with the outline panel absent, showing it disappears below a width threshold.

Colour is used so that One accent marks the written sources, the chapter sheets and their images. A second accent marks the two added theme files, script and stylesheet. A third accent marks everything generated, the finished page and the output folder.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 10 chapters in the table of contents; 9 entries in the sidebar order; 3 make targets; 2 added theme files; 1350 pixels, the width below which the outline hides.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: book, serve, clean, mdbook build, mdbook serve, book.toml, SUMMARY.md, right-menu.js, book/html, ayu, On this page.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: source chapters, SUMMARY.md, mdbook build, book.toml, chapter sidebar, On this page, ayu dark theme, rendered page section headings, outline links, active link, narrow window, hidden outline book, serve, clean, mdbook serve book/html, static HTML, browser preview, optional deploy markdown sources, page images, right-menu.js, stylesheet, rebuild on change, ignored output

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Each chapter is one markdown file; Contents file sets the sidebar order; Two theme files ride along with every build. Outline lists second-level headings only; Highlight follows the reader down the page. serve cleans, rebuilds, then opens locally; clean deletes the built folder. Output is plain files, no runtime needed. Touching any source triggers another build.
